messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

The user wants to find libraries in three cities with certain facilities. We need to call the function multiple times. The function signature expects location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated strings? Wait the type says facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; That seems odd: It lists union types but also array? Actually it might mean facilities can be one of those strings or an array of them? But the example shows "Cafe"[] meaning array of Cafe? Might be mis-specified. We'll just pass each facility separately? The function likely expects a single facility? But we need multiple. Maybe we should call function once per facility? Or maybe we can pass array of facilities? The type indicates "Cafe"[] means array of "Cafe"? So maybe we can pass array of strings? Let's assume we can pass array of facilities as list of strings.

We need to find libraries that have all specified facilities. So we need to call function with location and facilities list containing all required. For New York: Reading Room and Fiction. For Los Angeles: Wi-Fi and Children Section. For Chicago: Cafe and Reading Room.

We'll call function thrice.
